requirement_text.REQ-002: Replace every placeholder in messages/uz.json with real Uzbek translations. Acceptance criteria: (1) every key has a non-empty value not byte-identical to ru.json's corresponding value, except standalone domain-vocabulary terms (none found in this catalog); (2) no Cyrillic characters anywhere in messages/uz.json; (3) status-label-shaped values render correctly per the design's casing convention (confirmed CSS-driven uppercase, so lowercase JSON values are correct); (4) no exclamation marks, slogans, or emoji anywhere in messages/uz.json.

task.description: Run the scope test first: this requirement has real user-visible surface (rendered Uzbek copy across all 12 sections) -- continue to the full procedure. Write docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-002.md covering REQ-002's 4 acceptance criteria with mechanically precise checks: (1) a node script comparing every ru.json/uz.json key pair, flagging any byte-identical value (expect zero, since REVIEWER already confirmed no placeholders remain); (2) a Cyrillic-regex scan over messages/uz.json (expect zero matches); (3) a grep for exclamation marks/common emoji ranges in messages/uz.json (expect zero); (4) a curl+grep check on /uz confirming the page renders with real Uzbek strings (pick 3-4 spot-check strings from different namespaces, read the actual current messages/uz.json to get real expected values) and no next-intl error markers; (5) npm run build clean. Since REQ-001b's test spec already established the pattern for checking next-intl rendering, follow a similar structure but scoped to translation-content correctness rather than mechanism correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-002's 4 acceptance criteria has at least one verification case
Each case names the exact command and exact expected output

result.summary: Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-002.md covering REQ-002's 4 acceptance criteria plus a supporting rendered-page check, all commands run against the current codebase to capture real expected output before writing them into the spec. AC1 (node script diffing every ru.json/uz.json key pair): 177 keys, empty_uz_values: [], identical_value_pairs lists exactly 21 keys, each independently confirmed to be a standalone domain-vocabulary/proper-noun/brand term (event codes, country/role labels, URLs, NPS, brand name) per REQ-002's own exception clause -- zero real-copy leftovers. AC2 (Cyrillic regex scan): cyrillic_matches: 0. AC3 (status-label casing): confirmed globals.css line 152 `.status{text-transform:uppercase}` applies unconditionally, and the 8 rendered status spans on /uz are lowercase Uzbek words as expected. AC4 (exclamation marks + emoji scan): zero exclamation marks; emoji scan initially flagged the plain typographic arrow U+2192 (used 9x identically in both locales as a UI afford, not an emoji) as a false positive from an overly broad Unicode arrows range -- narrowed the regex to actual emoji/dingbat/symbol blocks only, re-ran: emoji_matches: 0. AC5 (npm run build): exit 0, '✓ Compiled successfully', zero lines matching case-insensitive 'error'. Supporting check: curl+grep on /uz confirms zero MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError markers (control-checked against /ru too) and 4 real Uzbek spot-check strings across 4 distinct namespaces (Nav, Hero t.rich() em, Doors, Footer) render correctly, including a t.rich() em-tag rendering check and an anchored Footer.about check that avoids a false double-match against the page's embedded RSC JSON payload. No TODOs left in the spec.
